events.label: FOMC Decision (2pm ET) + Warsh press conf (2:30pm) + META Q2 AH + MSFT Q4 FY26 AH — most event-dense session of 2026
events.note: Updated July 28 night: FOMC rate decision 2pm ET, Warsh press conference 2:30pm, then META Q2 AH and MSFT Q4 FY26 AH in the same session. Warsh inherits: (1) Brent $84.09 — first close below $85 regime trigger since Iran conflict began; (2) WTI $79.26, $0.26 above $79 clearance threshold; (3) 30Y at 5.10% (still above 5.00% trigger); (4) September hike prob ~70% near the formal trigger; (5) Durable Goods +0.3% vs. +2.5% expected (dovish). The language on September — not the hold decision itself — is the true binary. Dovish (September de-emphasized): TLT rally, upgrade clock potentially starts Day 1 if SPX closes above 7,480. Hawkish (September explicitly live): 30Y tests 5.20%, SPX tests 7,380 BEARISH threshold. THEN: META Q2 (EPS est $7.18, Rev est $60.22B; operating margin vs. AI capex is the swing) and MSFT Q4 FY26 (Azure 40%+ growth vs. $262B FY27 CapEx — GOOGL −7% template risk if capex guides without credible AI ROI). MSFT Azure guidance at 42%+ is the chip sector's most important near-term demand signal: it determines whether NVDA circular financing is product financing (demand real) or closed-loop demand subsidization (demand artificial).

events.label: AAPL Q2 AH + AMZN Q2 AH + Q2 GDP Advance Estimate (8:30 AM ET) — final Mag-7 and first GDP read
events.note: Updated July 28 night: Three catalysts in one session. Q2 GDP advance estimate at 8:30am ET (est. +2–3% annualized) — below +2% opens stagflation discussion; above +3% eases hard-landing concern. AAPL Q2 AH: AAPL hit a NEW ALL-TIME CLOSING HIGH at $340.08 Tuesday (+1.0%), now largest US company by market cap. Quality rotation into AAPL is confirmed in two consecutive sessions. China iPhone units, services gross margin (est. >73%), and Q3 revenue guidance (est. >$107B) are the three confirmation metrics. EPS est $1.89, Rev est $108.9B. Brent clearing $85 is directly constructive for China supply chain costs. AMZN Q2 AH: AWS est. +32% growth — if AWS confirms AI inference demand is volume-additive (Kimi K3 day-0 hosted on Together AI and Modal), AMZN's inference-demand beneficiary thesis strengthens. EPS est $1.82, Rev est $196.7B. If AAPL China beats AND AMZN AWS confirms +30%+ AI demand growth AND Q2 GDP above +2%: upgrade clock potentially Day 2 by Friday July 31 close.

events.label: PCE deflator + Employment Cost Index — June inflation embedded in end-of-month data
events.note: Updated July 28 night: PCE captures June Brent $97–100 oil inputs (2–3 week lag to gasoline component) plus early tariff pass-through from Trump's 10–12.5% duties on 99.4% of US imports (effective July 24). Employment Cost Index is the Fed's preferred wage inflation measure. An above-consensus PCE or ECI re-anchors the August 13 CPI concern even if FOMC was dovish Wednesday. By Friday's close, the briefing will know FOMC language, five Mag-7 Q2 prints, and one GDP advance read — the full information set to determine whether the regime formally upgrades, holds Step Aside, or converts to BEARISH.

events.label: PLTR Q2 2026 earnings AH — options pricing a 15% swing

PLTR insulated from AI circular financing narrative due to government contract revenue base (DoD AI spending secular). Key metrics: AIP commercial ARR growth, U.S. commercial customer count, and government contract expansion. DoD AI spending trajectory is independent of hyperscaler capex ROI debates. Weekend geopolitical risk (Iran ceasefire status) shapes Monday's pre-Palantir opening posture.

events.label: July CPI (est.) — Brent oil shock + Trump tariffs on 99.4% of imports; dual inflation embedding
events.note: Updated July 28 night: Two major inflation inputs, with Brent's July 28 clearance below $85 adding a new context. (1) Brent crude averaged ~$97–100 for multiple sessions before the Iran mutual pause; the July 14–24 high-Brent period is already embedded in July gasoline CPI. Tuesday's $84.09 Brent close means the retreat from $100.69 (Saturday July 26) to $84.09 (Tuesday July 28) will reduce the July gasoline component. Net July CPI oil contribution: still materially positive (the high-Brent period dominates the monthly average) but the retreat may limit pass-through to 3.0–3.5% vs. the 3.8%+ scenario if Brent had stayed above $90. (2) Trump's 10–12.5% tariffs on 99.4% of US imports (effective July 24) remain the second inflationary input. A July CPI print above 3.5% YoY still makes September near-certain regardless of Brent's current trajectory. Bull scenario (CPI ≤2.8%): oil pass-through was front-loaded and Brent's retreat dominates; September probability falls below 40%. Bear scenario (CPI ≥3.8%): dual oil+tariff pass-through exceeds expectations; September 50bps probability above 90%.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — circular financing disclosure + AMD hyperscaler sweep + Kimi K3 + CXMT questions
events.note: Updated July 28 night: NVDA Q2 FY27 is the fundamental clearing event for the AI GPU thesis. $91B revenue guidance represents sequential acceleration. NVDA recovered +0.4% Tuesday as institutional differentiation narrowed the AI chip trade to NVDA specifically while AMD fell 8.85%, Micron fell 8.4%. On the Q2 FY27 call, five questions must be addressed: (1) Circular financing disclosure — WSJ/Bloomberg active negotiation on $250B OpenAI backstop; analysts will press on whether Q2 revenue includes demand directly or indirectly financed by NVDA itself; (2) AMD hyperscaler diversification — all four major hyperscalers named as MI400 (Helios) customers; NVDA must quantify how much demand is AI-native vs. defensively captured; (3) Kimi K3 inference efficiency challenge (2.8T parameters, 70% API discount) — impact on per-token compute density and H100/H200 demand from inference-focused buyers; (4) CXMT Chinese DRAM competition — HBM3E demand is directly tied to NVDA data center orders; if CXMT is producing at government-backed scale, how does this affect the NVDA memory-order pipeline?; (5) China DUV lithography mass production — domestic Chinese tools accelerate CXMT's production ramp, tightening NVDA's China-exposure risk. Hard stop $216 intact.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off −13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst. Note: the NVDA circular financing story (July 27–28) — NVDA in talks to backstop $250B in OpenAI data center financing — adds complexity to the OpenAI IPO timeline if the guarantee structure is disclosed in S-1 filings.
